NOTICE FOR THE 52ND ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING
NOTICE  is hereby given that the 52nd Annual General Meeting of the 
members of RITES Limited will be held at 11:00 A.M. (IST) on Friday, 
September 25, 2026 through Video Conferencing (“VC”)/ Other 
Audio-Visual Means (“OAVM”) to transact the following business:
ORDINARY BUSINESS:
1. To receive, consider and adopt the Audited Financial Statements 
(Standalone and Consolidated) of the Company for the Financial 
Year ended March 31, 2026 along with the Board’s Report and 
Auditor's Report thereon and the comments of the Comptroller 
and Auditor General of India and in this regard, to consider 
and if thought fit, to pass, with or without modification(s), the 
following resolution as an Ordinary Resolution :
 “RESOLVED THAT the Audited Standalone and Consolidated 
Financial Statements of the Company for the financial year 
ended on March 31, 2026 along with the Board’s Report and 
Auditor's Report thereon and the comments of the Comptroller 
and Auditor General of India, as circulated to the members, be 
and are hereby considered and adopted.”
2. To confirm the payment of first, second and third interim 
dividend declared in the FY 2025-26 and to declare final 
dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended March 
31, 2026 and, in this regard, to consider and if thought fit, to 
pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolution 
as an Ordinary Resolution:
 “RESOLVED THAT approval of the members be and is hereby 
accorded to confirm the payment of first, second and third 
interim dividend @ 13%, 20% and 19% (H 1.30, H 2.00/- and  
H 1.90/- per equity share) on the paid-up equity share capital 
of the Company as approved by the Board and already paid in 
the month of August, 2025, November, 2025 and February, 
2026 respectively and to declare final dividend @ 27.50%  
(H 2.75/- per equity share) on the paid-up equity share capital of 
the Company for the financial year 2025-26, as recommended 
by the Board of Directors.”
3. To appoint a Director in place of Dr. Deepak Tripathi (DIN: 
10090267) Director (Technical), who retires by rotation as 
Director and being eligible, offers himself for re-appointment 
and in this regard, to consider and if thought fit, to pass, with 
or without modification(s), the following resolution as an 
Ordinary Resolution :
 “RESOLVED THAT in accordance with the provisions of Section 
152 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 
2013, Dr. Deepak Tripathi (DIN: 10090267), Director (Technical) 
who retires by rotation and being eligible offers himself for 
reappointment, be and is hereby reappointed as Director of the 
Company liable to retire by rotation.”4. To authorize the Board of Directors of the Company to fix the 
remuneration of the Statutory Auditors to be appointed by the 
Comptroller and Auditor General of India for the financial year 
2026-27 and in this regard, to consider and if thought fit, to 
pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolution 
as an Ordinary Resolution :
 “RESOLVED THAT pursuant to applicable provisions of the 
Companies Act, 2013, approval of the members be and is 
hereby accorded to authorize the Board of Directors of the 
Company to decide and fix the remuneration and out of pocket 
expenses payable to Statutory Auditors of the Company as may 
be appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India 
for the financial year 2026-27.”

NOTES:
1. Pursuant to General Circular Nos. 14/2020 dated April 8, 2020, 
17/2020 dated April 13, 2020, 20/2020 dated May 5, 2020, 
02/2022 dated May 5, 2022 and subsequent circulars issued in 
this regard, the latest being 3/2025 dated September 22, 2025, 
issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, (collectively referred 
to as MCA Circulars) and such other applicable circulars issued 
by MCA and Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) (the 
Circulars), the Company is convening its 52nd AGM through 
Video Conferencing (VC)/Other Audio Visual Means (OAVM) 
which does not require physical presence of members at a 
common venue. The deemed venue for the 52nd AGM shall be 
the Registered Office of the Company.
2. As per the provisions of Section 105 of the Companies Act, 
2013 (“Act”), a member entitled to attend and vote at AGM is 
entitled to appoint a proxy to attend and vote instead of himself/ 
herself and the proxy need not be a member of the Company. 
Since the AGM is being held through VC/ OAVM and physical 
attendance of members has been dispensed with, the facility 
for appointment of proxies by the members will not be available 
for the AGM. Accordingly, the Proxy Form, Attendance Slip and 
Route Map are not enclosed hereto. However, in pursuance of 
Section 112 and Section 113 of the Act, representatives of the 
Members may be appointed for the purpose of casting vote 
through remote e-Voting prior to the AGM, participation in the 
52nd AGM through VC/OAVM Facility and for electronic voting 
during the AGM.
3. Members attending the AGM through VC/OAVM shall be 
reckoned for the purpose of quorum for the AGM as per Section 
103 of the Act.
4. An Explanatory Statement pursuant to Section 102 of the Act 
relating to the Special Business, i.e. Item Nos. 5, 6, 7 and 8, to be 
transacted at the Annual General Meeting (‘AGM’) is annexed 
hereto. As per provisions of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
General Circular No. 20/2020 dated 5th May, 2020 the matters 
of Special Business as appearing in items nos. 5,6,7 and 8 of the 
above accompanying Notice, are considered to be unavoidable 
by the Board and hence, form part of this Notice.
5. Members under the category of Institutional Investors are 
encouraged to attend and vote at the AGM through VC/
OAVM. Corporate members are requested to send a scanned 
duly certified copy of the Board Resolution / Power of 
Attorney authorizing their representative to attend and vote 
on their behalf at the Annual General Meeting through VC/
OAVM. The said Resolution/Authorization should be sent to 
Company at cs@rites.com and to Scrutinizer for the AGM at 
asacs2022@gmail.com.
6. Brief resume of Directors seeking appointment/reappointment 
as prescribed under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with the Secretarial 
Standards issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of 
India is annexed hereto and forms part of the notice.7. The Members may join the AGM in the VC/OAVM mode 15 
minutes before the scheduled time of the commencement 
of the Meeting by following the procedure mentioned in the 
Notice. The facility of participation at the AGM through VC/ 
OAVM will be made available for 1000 members on first 
come first serve basis. This will not include large Shareholders 
(Shareholders holding 2% or more shareholding), Promoters, 
Institutional Investors, Directors, Key Managerial Personnel, 
the Chairpersons of the Audit Committee, Nomination and 
Remuneration Committee and Stakeholders Relationship 
Committee, Auditors etc. who are allowed to attend the AGM 
without restriction on account of first come first serve basis.
8. Members are advised to submit their Electronic Clearing System 
(ECS) mandates to enable the Company to make remittance by 
means of ECS. Those holding shares in dematerialized form may 
send the ECS Mandate to their Depository Participants (DP). 
Those who have already furnished the ECS Mandate Form 
to the Company/ Depository Participant/Registrar & Share 
Transfer Agent with complete details need not to send it again. 
Members holding shares in physical form may send the ECS 
Mandate Forms to the RTA of the Company.
9. Members holding shares in dematerialised form are requested 
to intimate all particulars of bank mandates, nominations, 
power of attorney, change of address, e-mail address, contact 
numbers, etc. to their Depository Participant (DP). Members 
holding shares in physical form are requested to intimate such 
details to the RTA of the Company.
 In order to enable the Company to remit dividend electronically 
through National Automated Clearing House (NACH), National 
Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT), etc., Members holding shares 
in physical form are requested to provide/update details of 
their bank accounts indicating the name of the bank, branch, 
account number and the nine digit MICR code and IFSC code 
(as appearing on the cheque) along with scanned copy of the 
cheque/ cancelled cheque at rites@beetalfinancial.com and 
beetalrta@gmail.com.
10. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has mandated 
the submission of Permanent Account Number (PAN) by every 
participant in securities market. Members holding shares in 
electronic form are, therefore, requested to submit their PAN to 
their Depository Participants with whom they are maintaining 
their demat accounts. Members holding shares in physical form 
can submit their PAN to the Company/RTA.
11. Non-Resident Indian members are requested to inform their 
Depository Participants, regarding:
 I. Change in their residential status on return to India for 
permanent settlement.
 II. Particulars of their bank account maintained in India with 
complete name, branch, account type, account number, 
IFSC Code and address of the Bank with pin code number, 
if not furnished earlier.

13. Pursuant to Section 139(5) of the Companies Act, 2013, the 
Auditors of a Government Company are appointed by the 
Comptroller and Auditor General (C&AG) of India and, in terms 
of provisions contained in Section 142 of the Companies 
Act 2013, their remuneration shall be fixed by the Company 
in a General Meeting or in such manner as the Company 
in a General Meeting may determine.  The members of the 
Company may authorise Board of Directors of the Company to 
fix the remuneration payable to Statutory Auditors as may be 
appointed by the C&AG for the FY 2026-27.

17. IEPF related information:
 Members are requested to note that dividends remaining 
unpaid/unclaimed for a period of 7 years from the date of 
transfer to Unpaid Dividend Account(s) of the Company are 
liable to be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection 
Fund (“IEPF”) of the Government of India.
 Pursuant to provisions of Companies Act, 2013, during financial 
year 2025-26, unclaimed final dividend for the financial year 
2017-18 and unclaimed 1st and 2nd interim dividend for the 
financial year 2018-19 have been transferred to Investor 
Education and Protection Fund (IEPF), established by Central 
Government. Pursuant to provisions of Investor Education 
and Protection Fund (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) 
Rules, 2016, the Company has uploaded the details of unpaid 
and unclaimed amounts lying with the Company on the website 
of the Company alongwith the list of shareholders whose 
unclaimed dividend are transferred to IEPF Authority.
 Further, Section 124(6) of the Act, provides that all shares in 
respect of which dividend has remained unpaid/unclaimed for 
7 consecutive years shall be transferred by the Company to the

MIRSDPOD/I/3750/2026 January 30, 2026, shareholders

from 5th February, 2026 to 4th February, 2027 for re-lodgement

Company’s website, and submission to the Stock Exchange(s).

To appoint Shri Prem Singh Meena (DIN: 10855590), as Whole Time 
Director [Director (Projects)] of the Company, liable to retire by 
rotation
As per the Article 56 of Articles of Association of the Company, the 
Hon’ble President of India, has the power to appoint Chairman/
Chairman & Managing Director of the Company, Whole time 
Functional Directors and other Directors.
Ministry of Railways vide its order No. 2025/E(O)II/40/6 dated 
March 19, 2026 has approved the appointment of Shri Prem Singh 
Meena (DIN: 10855590), Executive Director, RITES Limited as 
Director (Projects) of RITES Limited with effect from the date of 
assumption of charge of the post till the date of his superannuation 
i.e. 30.06.2028 or until further orders, whichever is earlier. Further, 
on the basis of recommendation of Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee, the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting 
held on March 19, 2026 has approved the appointment of Shri Prem 
Singh Meena (DIN: 10855590) as an Additional Director designated 
as Director (Projects) from the date of his assumption of charge to the 
post i.e. March 19, 2026.
In accordance with the proviso of Regulation 17(1C) of Securities 
and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI (LODR) Regulations”), 
a public sector company shall ensure that the approval of the 
shareholders for appointment or re-appointment of a person on the 
Board of Directors is taken at the next general meeting.
In terms of Sections 149, 152 and other applicable provisions, if any, 
of the Companies Act, 2013 (“Act”) and all the applicable provisions 
of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, the Company has received consent and 
requisite declaration & undertaking from Shri Prem Singh Meena 
(DIN: 10855590). As per the declaration/undertaking received, 
he is not disqualified from being appointed as Director in terms of 
provision of Section 164 of the Act and also not debarred by SEBI or 
any other authority from being appointed as a Director.The Company has received notice in writing from a Member under 
Section 160 of the Act proposing the candidature of Shri Prem 
Singh Meena (DIN: 10855590) for the office of Director (Projects) 
of the Company.
In view of the above, the Board of Directors of the Company  has 
recommended the appointment of Shri Prem Singh Meena (DIN: 
10855590) as Whole Time Director [Director (Projects)]) of the 
Company in accordance with Order No. 2025/E(O)II/40/6 dated 
19.03.2026 of the Ministry of Railways, Govt. of India and he shall be 
liable to retire by rotation.
A brief profile of Shri Prem Singh Meena (DIN: 10855590) in terms 
of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and Secretarial Standard-2, is 
annexed to this Notice. The terms & conditions of the appointment 
of Shri Prem Singh Meena (DIN: 10855590) are as per Ministry of 
Railways order dated March 19, 2026.
Except Shri Prem Singh Meena (DIN: 10855590), none of the 
Directors or Key Managerial Personnel or their relatives have any

(CMD) of the Company on 7th October, 2021. Subsequently, the 
appointment of Shri Rahul Mithal as Chairman & Managing Director 
(CMD) of the Company was approved by the shareholders of the 
Company by passing Ordinary Resolution through Postal Ballot.
In accordance with the proviso of Regulation 17(1C) of Securities 
and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI (LODR) Regulations”), 
a public sector company shall ensure that the approval of the 
shareholders for appointment or re-appointment of a person on the 
Board of Directors is taken at the next general meeting. 
Ministry of Railways, Government of India vide its letter No. 
2020/E(O)II/40/7 dated  August 20, 2026 has informed that the 
Competent Authority has approved the extension of tenure of 
appointment of Shri Rahul Mithal (DIN 07610499), Chairman & 
Managing Director, RITES Limited, beyond October 06, 2026 till the 
date of his superannuation i.e. June 30, 2027, or until further orders, 
whichever is earlier.As per  the declaration/undertaking received, he is not disqualified 
from being appointed/continuing as Director in terms of provision 
of Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013 and also not debarred 
by SEBI or any other authority from being appointed/continuing as 
a Director. As per the Articles of Association of the Company, the 
Chairman & Managing Director of the Company is a non-retiring 
Director and, accordingly, is not liable to retire by rotation.
In view of the above, the Board of Directors of the Company, 
has recommended the reappointment of Shri Rahul Mithal (DIN: 
07610499) as Chairman & Managing Director of the Company 
consequent to extension of tenure, not liable to retire by rotation in 
accordance with the letter no. 2020/E(O)II/40/7 dated August 20, 
2026 of the Ministry of Railways, Govt. of India. The Company has 
received notice in writing from a Member under Section 160 of the 
Act proposing the candidature of  Shri Rahul Mithal (DIN:07610499) 
for the office of Chairman & Managing Director of the Company.
A brief profile of Shri Rahul Mithal (DIN:07610499), Chairman 
& Managing Director of the Company in terms of SEBI (LODR) 
Regulations, 2015 and Secretarial Standard-2, is annexed to this

About The Report
This Integrated Annual Report provides a comprehensive account of RITES 
Limited’s performance and value creation journey for the financial year ended 
March 31, 2026. It offers an integrated perspective on how the Company 
harnessed its financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social and 
relationship, and natural capitals to drive business performance, strengthen 
stakeholder value and build a long-term growth.
The report presents a transparent and balanced overview of RITES 
Limited’s operating environment, strategic priorities, business 
performance, governance practices, risk management framework 
and sustainability initiatives. It highlights the opportunities and 
challenges that shaped the Company’s performance during the 
year, while outlining the strategic actions undertaken to navigate a 
dynamic business landscape.
Through this report, RITES Limited seeks to provide shareholders, 
clients, employees, business partners, lenders, regulators and 
other stakeholders with meaningful insights into its performance, 
priorities and approach to responsible value creation. It reflects the 
Company’s commitment to growth, while reinforcing its focus on 
creating enduring value for all stakeholders.
REPORTING FRAMEWORK
This report has been prepared in accordance with the International 
Integrated Reporting Framework issued by the IFRS Foundation. 
It explains the interrelationship between strategy, governance, 
performance, risks, opportunities and the six capitals that underpin 
the Company's business model.
The financial and statutory information presented in this report has 
been prepared in accordance with:
	  The Companies Act, 2013
	  Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
	  Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended
	  Secretarial Standards issued by The Institute of Company 
Secretaries of India
	  Other applicable statutory and Government requirements
Unless otherwise stated, the reporting boundary covers the 
standalone operations of RITES Limited. Environmental, Social and 
Governance (ESG) disclosures have been prepared in accordance 
with SEBI's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) 
framework, including applicable BRSR Core disclosures.AUDITORS’ REPORTS

under Section 143(6)(b) of the Companies Act, 2013, are NIL and

=== page 40 ===
Chairman & MD’s Message
Dear Shareholders,
As we look back at FY 2025–26, it truly marks a defining inflection 
point in RITES’ growth journey, and now providing a platform to 
surge ahead. Recognising the rapidly evolving ecosystem shaping 
both our domestic and international businesses, we went back to 
the drawing board, questioned the basics, leveraged our legacy 
knowledge and drafted a comprehensive business engineering plan. 
It required not just an operating model reset, not just a structural 
reset but a fundamental shift in mindset that we will take the 
challenge head-on and emerge successful, and we did.    
The key was our ability to secure orders consistently and on a 
competitive basis, maintaining a strike rate of ‘one order a day’ and 
building the highest-ever order book of ₹9,416 crore. The young 
order book has already begun generating revenue and we had 
turned the curve with a growth of 10% in the total revenue and a 
7% growth in the bottom line. 
In FY26, your Company achieved a consolidated revenue of ₹2525 
crore against ₹2302 crore in FY25. The operating revenue, excluding 
other income, stood at ₹2415 crore against ₹2196 crore in FY25. 
Profit Before Tax stood at ₹608 crore (₹565 crore in FY25), while 
Profit After Tax was ₹454 crore, compared to ₹424 crore in FY25. Not just these numbers, what was satisfying and reassuring was 
the revival of our export business after a gap of several years. The 
export orders secured  through global competitive tenders are now 
starting to contribute to the revenue. 
Consultancy continued to be the cornerstone of our business, 
contributing the highest-ever revenue of ₹1,310 crore. Our Leasing 
business saw a growth of 15%, achieving its highest-ever revenue of 
₹172 crore. The Turnkey revenue of ₹602 crore saw a dip primarily 
as the older orders were getting completed while the newer ones 
were only beginning to contribute to revenue. 
Giving impetus to ‘RITES Videsh’, a strategic initiative to strengthen 
our presence across key international markets, Regional Business 
Heads have been appointed for five strategic geographies, 
supported by operational offices in Manila, Abu Dhabi and 
Georgetown, while new offices in Johannesburg and Accra are being 
established. Together, these interventions reaffirm RITES’ growing 
stature as a trusted global partner in transport infrastructure and 
engineering consultancy. 
Our milestones this year reaffirmed what sets RITES apart — our 
ability to seamlessly integrate multidisciplinary expertise and deliver 
end-to-end infrastructure solutions, from concept to commissioning, 
across sectors, geographies and scales.Growth is rarely linear. It is built 
through step wise phases of business 
reengineering and consolidation, a test 
of the resilience of the organisation. 
For us, at RITES, FY 25-26 was the 
inflection point.
RITES Limited 20

WE SHAPE WHAT

best-in-class delivery.During the year, we completed diverse projects, including railway 
siding works for BPCL, NTPC and SECL, consultancy for the 
Bundelkhand and Gorakhpur Link Expressways, retro-fitment of 
RS-1 trains for Delhi Metro, General Engineering Consultancy for 
Ahmedabad Metro Phase-II, DPR for ropeways and the funicular 
system at Palani Temple, comprehensive health check-up of 
Rabindra Setu, 3D monitoring and construction supervision of six 
tunnels on the Jarati–Maligura doubling project, and supply of 10 
Cape Gauge locomotives to CFM Mozambique.
We also secured several strategic assignments, including Project 
Management Consultancy for IIM-Bengaluru Phase-I, TEFRs 
for greenfield airports at Amaravati and Srikakulam, DPR and 
transaction advisory for the Outer Harbour at Chennai Port, supply 
of five locomotives to Minas De Benga, Lda. (MBL), Mozambique, 
environmental and social monitoring for the Bengaluru Suburban 
Rail Project, and an IT-based transport model for the Ministry of 
Chemicals & Fertilizers.
Together, these projects underscore our diversified portfolio, 
expanding global footprint and proven capability to deliver high-
impact infrastructure solutions across domains.
Even amid margin pressures, your Company upheld its track record 
of delivering the highest dividend payout ratios while maintaining 
a robust balance sheet and healthy net worth. Reflecting this 
confidence, the Board of Directors has recommended ₹2.75 per 
share as a final dividend in addition to the three interim dividends, 
totaling ₹5.20 per share, which have already been paid during 
the year. The total dividend of ₹382 crore at ₹7.95 per share, on 
the accrual basis, takes the dividend payout ratio to 95.4% of the 
profits earned.
Your Company’s subsidiaries and joint ventures continued to 
strengthen the RITES portfolio, making meaningful contributions 
to our overall performance. REMC Ltd. recorded a substantial 
growth of 15.8% with the highest-ever total revenue of ₹163 crore 
& Profit After Tax of ₹90 crore and paid ₹83 crore as dividend. 
Continuing with its momentum, SRBWIPL reported the highest-
ever revenue of ₹379 crore and profit of ₹23 crore and paid a total 
dividend of ₹14 crore.
Our flagship CSR initiative ‘Changing Lives’, with a contribution 
of ₹11.80 crore in FY 26, reflects our commitment to creating 
meaningful social impact and value beyond business.   
Our achievements reflect the unwavering support of the Ministry 
of Railways and the trust of our stakeholders. As we surge ahead, 
the strength of our capabilities, the commitment of Team RITES, 
and the guidance of our Board remain our driving force. I extend my 
sincere gratitude to the Ministry, our esteemed Board, clients across 
geographies, valued investors, and the 3000+ members of Team 
RITES. Your trust and shared vision continue to shape our journey.
True enterprises recognise the moment when consolidation must 
transform into acceleration.  And we recognise that the next phase 
of growth will be driven not just by doing more of the same, but 
by much more of the new. As we increase the pace of growth in 
order book and profitability, we have already upped the curve and 
set ourselves a roadmap for integrating cutting-edge technology 
for best-in-class delivery. At RITES, we are clear that technology 
adoption is not merely for the sake of technology but with a purpose, leveraging our rich legacy to move from execution-
centric delivery to tech-driven solutions, and from scale alone 
to speed, quality and value creation. With this vision, we have 
created Abhikalp, our Centre of Excellence, fostering innovation, 
collaboration and the application of emerging technologies. This 
initiative will drive us to the next level, as we owe it to our rich 
legacy that we brook no compromise in quality and delivery, 
rededicating ourselves to our core values of ‘Operation Tattva: 
Quality, Cost & Time’. Our greatest strength has always been our 
people. As infrastructure becomes increasingly digital and AI-
driven, we are building a workforce that is ready for what’s next. 
Through learning initiatives such as our #aiReady initiative, we 
amplified AI adoption and equipped our team with the future-ready 
capabilities. The ‘Lakshya’ series is strengthening leadership and 
continuous learning, as these initiatives are building a more agile, 
future-ready RITES.
Anchored in a strong value system, your Company remains 
committed to the highest standards of corporate governance. 
Guided by ethical leadership, regulatory compliance, transparent 
decision-making and global best practices, RITES continues to 
strengthen stakeholder trust and create sustainable long-term value.
The curve ahead belongs to those who dare to redefine it. As we 
move forward, our ADAPT framework continues to guide our 
journey — acknowledging the change, strengthening capabilities, 
fostering partnerships, embracing technology and aligning our 
purpose with the evolving needs of the world. Backed by the trust 
of our stakeholders, the strength of our people and the confidence 
born of five decades of engineering excellence, we are ready not 
just to navigate the future, but to shape it—because at RITES:  
WE SHAPE WHAT SHAPES LIVES.
With Best Wishes,
Rahul Mithal

Approach to 
Value Creation
The transport infrastructure landscape is changing rapidly, driven by technology, 
rising client expectations, increasing competition and a stronger focus on 
efficiency and outcomes. As RITES moves from an expertise-led to a more 
market-led, technology-enabled and outcome-focused model, the opportunity is 
to build on its core strengths to create greater value for clients and stakeholders. 
In line with its purpose, We Shape What Shapes Lives , the Value Creation 
Framework seeks to translate RITES’ capabilities into sustainable growth, 
execution excellence and lasting impact.
RITES’ value creation approach is anchored in its core operational 
philosophy ‘Operation Tattva’, a disciplined framework that drives 
zero compromise on quality, optimal cost and timely delivery. These 
guiding principles are complemented by our strategic focus on 
sustainability, digital transformation, and client-centric solutions, 
enabling us to meet evolving market demands with agility.
For RITES, value creation is a continuous cycle of performance 
enhancement, relationship building, and operational excellence. 
A 5-point strategic approach designed to make RITES future-ready. ADAPT stands for:The RITES’ Way…
ADAPTLeveraging our multi-sector expertise, integrated project 
management, and prudent financial practices, we aim to strengthen 
competitiveness, resilience and long-term growth.
As we chart the curve, our value creation framework brings together 
our capabilities, strategic priorities and desired outcomes to deliver 
clear value for clients and stakeholders. It is built around two 
complementary dimensions: ADAPT and Operation Tattva.

=== page 66 ===
VISTARMAITRISAARTHI
VISTAR is an AI-enabled visual inspection system for railway 
assets that combines high-resolution imaging with AI-based 
defect detection to enhance inspection efficiency, accuracy and 
consistency. Deployed at SAIL Bhilai, the platform has evolved into a 
revenue-generating quality assurance service.MAITRI (Master Application for International Trade and Regulatory 
Interface) is a digital platform designed as a ‘Virtual Trade Corridor’ 
for seamless cross-border data exchange. By integrating port 
and customs systems across countries, MAITRI enables secure 
and efficient sharing of logistics data, supporting smoother trade 
processes and greater transparency across borders.SAARTHI (Smart and Automated Review, Tracking & Holistic 
Inspection) is a technology-driven portal that enables real-time 
monitoring of railway inspections. From vendor benchmarking to 
automated alerts and centralised quality monitoring, it enhances 
transparency, efficiency and oversight—enabling faster decisions 
and safer, more reliable rail systems.Governing Innovation
At RITES, we institutionalise innovation through defined governance 
mechanisms, converting ideas into approved workflows and 
standardised tools supported by periodic reviews, standardisation 
committees and project close-out learning. This structured approach 
enables us to move from experimentation to implementation, as 
demonstrated by solutions such as VISTAR, MAITRI and SAARTHI, 
which leverage AI, digital technologies and data to enhance quality, 
efficiency, transparency and decision-making.
OPTIMISING RESOURCES
Optimisation is central to our approach to advancing sustainability 
across large-scale infrastructure projects. By leveraging our physical 
assets, advanced technologies and engineering expertise, we 
enhance operational efficiency while integrating environmental 
considerations into project planning and delivery. This enables us to 
balance resource efficiency, operational performance and long-term 
sustainability across our projects.

environment. The revised policy broadens the scope of risk oversight to address cyber security, sustainability-related risks and emerging 
regulatory developments, while providing a structured process for identifying, assessing, mitigating, monitoring and reporting risks across the 
organisation. The framework is supported by a five-tier governance structure that establishes clear accountability and oversight at every level.

The Financial Year 2025–26 marked a phase of resilient execution and broad-based growth for RITES. Building on its established 
engineering and consultancy strengths, the Company sharpened its focus on high-value project consultancy, export revival, 
strategic partnerships and technology-enabled delivery. During the year, RITES continued to strengthen its domestic and 
international presence while responding effectively to evolving market requirements across transport infrastructure, logistics 
and allied sectors.
During FY25–26, the Company recorded a consolidated total revenue of H2,525 crore, with operating revenue of H2,415 crore, 
and Profit After Tax (PAT) of H454 crore. Consolidated operating revenue grew by about 10% year-on-year and PAT increased 
by 7.3%, reflecting improved execution, a better revenue mix and sustained operational discipline. EBITDA also improved to  
H568 crore, with margins remaining healthy at 23.5%. On a standalone basis, the Company achieved a total revenue of H2,426 
crore, and a profit after tax of H401 crore.

provided consultancy services.

Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 53
The Company ended the year with an all-time high order book of  
H9,416 crore as on March 31, 2026, providing strong visibility for 
future revenues. During the year, the Company continued to maintain 
a strike rate of securing one order a day, thereby underscoring the 
continued trust of clients across consultancy, turnkey, leasing and 
export businesses.
With a growing emphasis on integrated, resilient and sustainable 
transport networks, RITES is well positioned to benefit from 
opportunities in technical consultancy, asset-light project execution 
and the export of indigenously developed rolling stock. Guided by its 
ADAPT framework and supported by a strengthened workforce, the 
Company continues to demonstrate agility, innovation and operational 
resilience, positioning itself for sustained growth in the years ahead.
State of Company’s Affairs & Outlook
FY 25-26 was a year in which focused execution and strategic 
adaptability translated into improved performance across RITES’ 
major business lines. Project Consultancy remained the principal 
revenue driver, contributing H1,185 crore and reaffirming its central 
role in the Company’s operating model. The Turnkey and Leasing 
verticals also delivered steady contributions of H602 crore and  
H172 crore, respectively, reflecting RITES’ ability to execute diverse 
assignments with consistency.
One of the most notable developments during the year was the 
revival of the Export segment, which generated revenues of H316 
crore after a period of subdued activity. This recovery was led by 
the successful supply of all 10 cape-gauge locomotives to CFM 
Mozambique under a globally competitive mandate, marking an 
important validation of RITES’ international execution capabilities. 
Bolstering our global footprint, RITES has successfully secured a 
major H915 crore contract to supply 200 broad-gauge passenger 
coaches to Bangladesh Railway. Project execution is advancing on schedule, with the initial delivery of a 20-coach rake slated for the 
forthcoming financial year. The Company also continued its outreach 
across Africa, South Asia and other overseas markets under its RITES 
Videsh initiative, strengthening its global positioning.
RITES further expanded its collaborative footprint through strategic 
MoUs and partnerships with the Government of Botswana, CONCOR, 
SAIL, and DP World. These engagements broadened the Company’s 
capabilities in railway modernisation, logistics infrastructure, 
locomotive leasing, data-driven advisory and integrated transport 
solutions. The strategic shift toward collaborative and higher-margin 
consultancy opportunities helped offset external pressures and 
reinforced the Company’s focus on high-impact, scalable execution.
The Company’s subsidiaries and joint ventures, including REMC 
Limited, SAIL-RITES Bengal Wagon Industry Private Limited 
(SRBWIPL) and RITES (Afrika) (Proprietary) Limited, continued to 
contribute to consolidated performance during the year. These 
entities supported RITES’ wider capabilities in green energy 
procurement, wagon manufacturing and international project 
delivery, adding resilience and depth to the overall business portfolio.
RITES’ subsidiary REMC Limited, which has a mandate  to handle the 
power procurement under ‘open access’ for Indian Ra ilways, besides 
handling renewable energy and energy- efficiency pr ojects, achieved 
total income of H162.74 crore and profit after tax of H90.15 crore during 
the year. It paid an interim dividend of H65.10 crore ( H6.20 per share) 
and the REMC’s Board of Directors has recommended f inal dividend of 
H17.85 crore ( H1.70 per share), subject to the approval of shareho lders.
During the financial year, RITES’ Joint Venture, SAIL-RITES Bengal 
Wagon Industry Private Limited, manufactured 1089 wagons (954 
BOXNHL and 135 BOXNR). It clocked total income of H379.44 crore 
and profit after tax of H 22.59 crore. An interim dividend of H14.40 crore  
(H3.00 per share) was distributed.

 As per the provisions of Section 197 (12) of the Companies 
Act, 2013 read with Rule 5 of the Companies (Appointment 
and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014, 
every listed Company is required to disclose the ratio of the 
remuneration of each Director to the median employee’s 
remuneration and details of employees receiving remuneration 
exceeding the limit as prescribed from time to time in the 
Board’s Report.
 However, as per notification dated 05.06.2015 issued by the 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), Government Companies 
are exempted from complying with the provisions of Section 
197 of the Companies Act, 2013. Therefore, such particulars 
have not been included as a part of Board’s Report.

Conservation of Energy, Technology Absorption and 
Foreign Exchange Earnings and Outgo
Conservation of Energy
As a consultancy organization, RITES’ operations are primarily office-
based and do not involve energy-intensive manufacturing activities. 
Nevertheless, the Company remains committed to the efficient 
utilization of energy and conservation of natural resources through 
various sustainability initiatives across its offices and campuses.
RITES’ decarbonisation journey is supported through green buildings, 
operational energy efficiency, green IT initiatives and renewable 
energy transition. During the year, focused efforts were made to 
enhance energy efficiency through a combination of operational 
improvements and infrastructure upgrades aimed at optimising 
energy consumption, reducing carbon emissions and supporting 
national energy conservation goals while ensuring environmental, 
financial and human capital efficiency.
Energy Efficiency and Optimisation
The Company continued to implement various measures to improve 
energy performance across its facilities, including:
	  Development of new offices in accordance with green building 
standards and adoption of innovative technologies.
	  Optimisation of operational energy efficiency through real-time 
monitoring and intelligent control systems through building 
management system.
	  Upgradation and replacement of legacy equipment and utilities 
with energy-efficient alternatives.
As a result of these initiatives, the following achievements were 
recorded during the year:
	  Reduction in overall energy consumption by 
approximately 1.42%.
	  Increase in renewable energy utilisation by approximately 222%.
	  Reduction in diesel consumption by approximately 59% at 
Shikhar and Srijan.Steps Taken for Energy Conservation
Solar Power Deployment
In furtherance of RITES’ commitment towards energy conservation 
and adoption of renewable energy sources, a rooftop solar power 
plant of 120 kWp capacity was installed and commissioned at the 
newly constructed Regional Project Office, Lucknow.
Further augmentation of the existing solar infrastructure is under 
progress through enhancement of rooftop solar capacities at:
	  Shikhar: from 25 kWp to 70 kWp
	  Srijan: from 10 kWp to 18 kWp
In addition, rooftop solar power plants aggregating 138 kWp capacity 
were commissioned at the Regional Project Office, Kolkata and 
Vishranti (Rest House), Gurugram. These initiatives strengthen the 
Company's renewable energy portfolio and reinforce its commitment 
towards sustainable operations, reduction of carbon footprint and 
alignment with the Government of India's clean energy and green 
growth objectives.
Smart Energy Management Systems
Both newly constructed offices, including Kolkata and Lucknow, have 
been equipped with advanced Building Management Systems for 
real-time monitoring and control of building services. Smart metering 
systems and DALI sensor-controlled lighting have also been deployed 
to optimise energy consumption.
Energy-efficient motors and equipment compliant with the Energy 
Conservation Building Code (ECBC) standards have been installed to 
further enhance operational efficiency.
Operational Controls
Group-controlled elevator systems have been installed in all 
newly constructed offices and Shikhar to optimise lift operations, 
minimise passenger waiting time and reduce energy consumption 
during peak hours.
The lifts at Shikhar are further integrated with cloud-based monitoring 
systems that enable predictive maintenance by continuously tracking 
operational performance, reducing unplanned downtime and 
enhancing passenger safety.
Other Cost Optimisation Measures
Additional energy conservation measures undertaken during 
the year include:
	  Maximisation of natural daylight utilisation.
	  Maintaining air-conditioning temperatures in the 
range of 24–25°C.
	  Sealing of doors and windows to minimise cooling losses.
	  Regular preventive maintenance of air-conditioning systems 
and electrical equipment.
	  Reduction of plug-load demand through shared use of 
appliances and equipment.

Technology Absorption
Technology continues to be a key driver of innovation, operational 
excellence, and sustainable growth at RITES. During the year, the 
Company strengthened its technology ecosystem by integrating 
advanced digital engineering practices, Artificial Intelligence (AI), 
Industry 4.0 technologies, intelligent automation, and data-driven 
solutions across its business verticals. These initiatives are aimed at 
enhancing project delivery, improving quality and safety, increasing 
operational efficiency, and creating new technology-enabled service 
offerings for clients.
Recognizing the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence, 
RITES launched the #AIReady RITES initiative to build an intelligent, 
innovative, and future-ready organization. The initiative seeks to 
promote AI awareness, strengthen institutional capabilities, enable 
data-driven decision-making, and foster responsible adoption of 
emerging technologies across the organization.
A major milestone during the year has been the establishment 
of the Abhikalp – Centre of Excellence (CoE), envisioned as the 
central innovation hub for Artificial Intelligence and allied Industry 
4.0 technologies. The Centre aims to accelerate the adoption of AI, 
Digital Twin, Building Information Modeling (BIM), Computer Vision, 
Internet of Things (IoT), Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), 
3D Printing, advanced analytics, and intelligent automation across 
engineering consultancy, quality assurance, project monitoring, and 
enterprise support functions. It will serve as a collaborative platform 
for developing, validating, and demonstrating technology-driven 
solutions before their large-scale deployment across RITES and for 
client projects.
The Company has initiated the development of PARAKH, an AI-
enabled platform for appraisal and evaluation of Detailed Project 
Reports (DPRs). The platform is designed to assist domain experts 
in analyzing complex technical, financial, environmental, contractual, 
and regulatory documents through intelligent document processing, 
automated validation, knowledge retrieval, and decision-support 
capabilities, while maintaining a human-in-the-loop approach for 
critical technical assessments.
In the field of Quality Assurance, RITES has continued to advance AI-
based inspection systems. VISTAR (Visual Inspection System Through 
AI for Rails) leverages computer vision and artificial intelligence to 
support automated inspection of rails by detecting surface defects 
with enhanced speed, consistency, and accuracy. Similar AI-
enabled visual inspection solutions are being explored for other 
safety-critical railway components, further strengthening RITES' 
inspection capabilities.

Environment Protection
RITES demonstrates a strong commitment to sustainability by 
embedding environmental responsibility, resource efficiency, and 
green practices across its operations and consultancy services. The 
organization promotes eco-friendly development through initiatives 
in renewable energy, energy-efficient systems, green buildings, 
sustainable water and waste management, and digitalization aimed at 
reducing environmental impact.
As a leading infrastructure consultancy, RITES undertakes Feasibility 
Studies, Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), and Environmental & Social 
Impact Assessments (ESIAs) in compliance with national regulations 
issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 
(MoEF&CC) as well as international standards prescribed by agencies 
such as the World Bank, ADB, JICA, and EIB. This ensures that 
sustainability objectives and mitigation measures are integrated 
throughout the entire project lifecycle.
In line with its sustainable development vision, RITES has expanded 
its expertise into areas such as solid and used water management, 
clean air initiatives, ESG and BRSR activities, pollution control, 
lake and river rejuvenation, net-zero studies, wetland management 
planning, green and environmental compliance audits, eco-sensitive 
zone management plans, and green mobility solutions.
The Company’s sustainability-driven approach is further 
strengthened through strategic collaborations with institutions 
including Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur for air quality 
management, Indian Institute of Technology Madras for green 
hydrogen and clean energy innovation, and National Institute of Solar 
Energy for renewable energy initiatives. RITES also functions as the 
Technical Support Unit under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0 for 
the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, contributing to legacy waste 
management, sludge treatment, water reuse, and standardization of 
urban sanitation systems.
Beyond consultancy services, RITES has incorporated sustainability 
into its own organizational practices. Its Gurugram office complex, 
“Srijan,” has been awarded the GRIHA Gold Standard rating, while its 
Kolkata office has received a four-star GRIHA Pre-Certification. The 
Company has implemented several energy-efficiency measures across 
its offices, including solar power systems, LED lighting, skylights, 
and sensor-based fixtures. These initiatives are complemented 
by rainwater harvesting systems, sewage treatment plants, and 
adherence to all applicable emission and waste management norms.The Company is also expanding the application of Structural 
Health Monitoring Systems (SHMS) for continuous monitoring of 
bridges, buildings, tunnels, and other critical infrastructure assets. 
By integrating sensors, IoT, analytics, and AI-based predictive 
models, SHMS facilitates real-time condition assessment, 
predictive maintenance, improved asset reliability, and enhanced 
lifecycle management.
Technology absorption has also been strengthened through the 
development of enterprise digital platforms and AI-powered internal 
solutions. AI-based digital assistants, including Tele Sathi, IT Sathi, 
HR Sathi, and Query Sathi, are being implemented to improve 
employee services, automate routine processes, enhance knowledge 
management, and improve organizational productivity. Digital 
workflows, SAP-based enterprise systems, analytics dashboards, 
intelligent document processing, and workflow automation continue 
to strengthen governance, transparency, and operational efficiency.
Across engineering business verticals, RITES has expanded the use 
of advanced digital technologies including Building Information 
Modeling (BIM), Digital Twin, GIS, drone-based surveys, LiDAR 
mapping, cloud-based collaboration platforms, advanced simulation 
tools, and 3D Printing. These technologies are being utilized for 
infrastructure planning, engineering design, digital visualization, 
project monitoring, quantity estimation, asset management, and 
lifecycle optimization across railways, highways, bridges, buildings, 
airports, ports, and urban infrastructure projects.
The Company is also exploring AI-enabled solutions for tender 
intelligence, bid management, engineering knowledge management, 
predictive analytics, computer vision-based inspection, document 
intelligence, and digital decision-support systems to enhance 
business development and improve project execution capabilities.
Recognizing that technology transformation is driven by people, 
RITES has undertaken significant initiatives towards AI literacy 
and digital capability development. Organisation-wide training 
programs on Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot, 
Prompt Engineering, and emerging digital technologies have been 
conducted to build awareness and enhance workforce readiness. 
The introduction of AI Ambassadors across departments is expected 
to further accelerate innovation, facilitate adoption of emerging 
technologies, and promote a culture of continuous learning.
Through sustained investments in technology absorption, digital 
innovation, and capability development, RITES continues to 
strengthen its position as a technology-enabled multidisciplinary 
engineering consultancy. The Company remains committed to 
leveraging emerging technologies to deliver smarter, safer, more 
sustainable, and future-ready infrastructure solutions while creating 
long-term value for its clients and stakeholders.

Risk Management
In compliance with Regulation 21 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 
2015, the Board of Directors of the Company has constituted a 
Risk Management Committee which acts in accordance with its 
terms of reference and oversees Risk Management Framework 
which lays down the procedures about the risk management and 
mitigation thereof.
The Company follows a consistent and comprehensive risk 
management strategy at all levels. Each Vertical/Region has a risk 
management team to assess and mitigate risks at the operational 
level. Decisions taken on risk mitigation are implemented and 
reviewed regularly for effectiveness, for which a rigorous system of 
audits by internal as well as external auditors exists.
Company’s Risk Management procedure covers all aspects which may 
affect its working like, changes in business environment, Government 
policies, competency requirements, manpower planning, safety of 
manpower, buildings and other assets, currency risk management, 
data security, cyber security etc.
In compliance with Section 134(3)(n) of the Companies Act, 2013 and 
Regulation 17(9) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, the Company 
had a Risk Management Policy and framework in place which has 
been revised with the Board of Directors approval during the year. 
The same is available on the website of the company. This enhances 
the structured framework for the identification, assessment, 
mitigation, monitoring and reporting of risks across the organisation. 
The Risk Management Framework is reviewed periodically by the Risk 
Management Committee and the Board of Directors to ensure its 
continued effectiveness and alignment with the Company’s strategic 
objectives, business environment and regulatory requirements. 
The Company maintains the Risk Library for all the identified risk and 
their mitigation plan for easy reference. 
Further, Company’s Risk Management procedure covers all aspects 
which may affect its working like, changes in business environment, 
Government policies, competency requirements, manpower 
planning, safety of manpower, buildings and other assets, currency 
risk management, data security, cyber security etc. The Company is

System Certification (ISO 9001:2015) & QA 
Accreditations
RITES Limited has been certified under the ISO 9000 series of Quality 
Management System (QMS) standards since 1999. The current system 
is documented in accordance with ISO 9001:2015 requirements.
The QMS framework includes Monitoring and Analysis of 
Organizational activities, as a result, it forms an integral part of 
the Company’s internal control mechanisms. The system ensures 
delivery of high-quality service, promotes operational excellence, 
and supports continual improvement and effective risk management, 
aligning with international best practices. 
RITES ISO 9001:2015 certification has been awarded by M/s 
NVT Quality Certification International LLP, Bangalore (NVTQC), 
accredited by ANAB (ANSI National Accreditation Board).
During FY 2025-26, RITES successfully enhanced its Quality 
Management System (QMS) awareness and competence through the 
organization of QMS Lead Auditor and Internal Auditor programs for 
working employees, introductory ISO 9001:2015 training for newly 
inducted staff. 
In addition, the RITES QA Vertical is also accredited to ISO 
17020:2012 & ISO 17065: 2012 by the National Accreditation Board 
for Certification Bodies (NABCB), a constituent of the Quality Council 
of India (QCI). This accreditation ensures that inspection services are 
aligned with international standards.
The QA Vertical also operates material testing laboratories across 
various Regional Inspection Offices, which are accredited as per ISO 
17025:2017 by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and 
Calibration Laboratories (NABL), a constituent of the Quality Council 
of India (QCI).
Now, the QA Vertical is also a member of the TIC Council, Belgium. 
TIC Council is an international association representing independent 
testing, inspection and certification companies. Membership enhances RITES’ global visibility and alignment with international 
practices in the TIC industry.

Knowledge Management System
RITES’ has established a robust Knowledge Management System 
(KMS) that leverages the organisation’s collective expertise and 
institutional knowledge to drive operational excellence, innovation, 
and future readiness. The system is designed to systematically 
capture, preserve, share, and enhance knowledge across the 
enterprise, ensuring that valuable insights and experiences remain 
accessible for current and future generations of employees.
Knowledge assets are securely maintained through a suite of in-house 
digital platforms and specialised repositories. These include the 
project-focussed Document Management System ‘ NIDHI ’, the SAP-
enabled financial dashboard ‘ DARPAN ’, domain-specific databases, 
Board Meeting Management Systems, and various employee-centric 
portals. Together, these platforms provide a centralized, reliable, 
and easily accessible repository of organisational information, 
enabling informed decision-making and seamless collaboration 
across functions.
To further strengthen knowledge accessibility, RITES has implemented 
a dedicated CV Dashboard that serves as a comprehensive repository 
of employee competencies and professional profiles. Equipped with 
advanced search and filtering capabilities, the platform facilitates 
the efficient identification of subject matter experts and skilled

professionals, ensuring optimal resource deployment and improved 
project outcomes.
Recognising that knowledge management extends beyond knowledge 
preservation, RITES places significant emphasis on continuous 
learning and capability development. The Training Portal ‘ SAKSHAM ’ 
acts as a centralized learning platform, offering employees access 
to a wide range of training programmes, presentations, technical 
resources, and recorded sessions. The portal empowers employees 
to continuously upgrade their skills and competencies, fostering a

Through these integrated initiatives, RITES has created a

remain agile and future-ready in an evolving business environment.
Human Resources and Industrial Relations
Being a leading transport infrastructure consultancy and engineering 
Company, RITES is constantly looking to enhance its knowledge 
capabilities and professional pool by inducting bright, qualified 
employees into its team every year. In line with this mission, the Human 
Resource Department of RITES is committed to achieve excellence in 
talent acquisition, upskilling & training, employee engagement, talent 
retention, career progression and development of human capital. The 
Company’s progressive HR policies have a purpose-driven approach 
of being established as an “Equal Opportunity Employer”. Such 
policies are one of the many reasons there is an ease in employee 
acquisition, retention and maintenance of a very low attrition rate. 
The attrition rate of regular employees during FY25-26 was 2.76%.
As a part of succession planning and career progression, as well as to 
keep the employee motivated, a periodic review of cadres is done. The 
reviews are conducted in a supportive environment, with benchmarks 
outlined against the business goals of the Company and best practices 
in the industry.
During FY25-26, the selection process of 604 eligible candidates 
from across disciplines, levels & regions was conducted, and 327 
employees (including both executive & non-executive staff) were 
promoted. The Company believes in consistently improving its 
systems and processes to attract, motivate and nurture talent. It 
focuses on making the workforce agile and future ready to align with 
dynamic industry trends and the infrastructure needs of tomorrow.

continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and employee capability

access learning opportunities anytime and anywhere. It empowers 
employees to nominate themselves for relevant courses, and maintain

professional growth, and fosters a culture of lifelong learning across 
the organization, thereby strengthening the overall capability and 
competitiveness of RITES' workforce.
Implementation of Right to Information Act, 2005 (RTI)
RITES has put in place a robust implementation structure with 
high level of commitment towards transparency amongst the First 
Appellate Authority (FAA), Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) 
& Assistant Central Public Information Officers (ACPIOs) which had 
profound influence on successful implementation and accomplishing 
goals & objectives of the Right to Information Act, 2005. By 
establishing citizens’ right to have maximum access to records & 
documents in all areas, barring a limited regime of exceptions, has 
thus improved transparency, accountability, good governance and 
service delivery.
To bring about transparency in RITES’s administrative culture, 
concerted efforts were made through in house awareness and training 
programmes for officers & staff highlighting the significance and 
strategic approach with which RITES is pursuing the implementation 
of the Right to Information Act, 2005. This has helped in a catalytic 
improvement in implementing the Act, making the goals & objectives 
achievable with their concerted, creative and decisive actions.
RITES believes in the principle of “maximum disclosure”, the 
right to access information extends to a broad range of records & 
documents unless specifically included in the narrowly defined list 
of exemptions. Therefore, in RITES, there is a fundamental paradigm 
shift, a presumption of disclosure and transparency supersedes the 
presumption of secrecy and the effective implementation of the Right 
to Information Act, 2005, has fostered a new culture of openness.
RITES has been putting sincere efforts in creating informed citizenry 
& promoting transparency through pro-active disclosures on its 
website under Section 4(1)(b) of the Right to Information Act, 2005. 
Categories of information frequently sought, have also been identified, 
catalogued, and organized in a retrievable user-friendly database. 
RITES conducts Transparency Audit regularly to ensure compliance 
of all the stipulated major statutory requirements of Section 4 of the 
Right to Information Act and compliances for DoPT OM/Circular 
dated April 15, 2013 for proactive/Suo-Motu disclosures and other 
provisions of the Right to Information Act.
The provision for submission of RTI applications/First Appeals with 
payment of application/additional fee online, provided on RITES 
website, has enabled citizens to file their applications/First Appeals 
with ease and receive information faster, cutting on the cost of postal 
dispatch and nullifying the time of postal transit.
The gradual reduction in the number of new applications highlights 
the effective use of RITES’ Website and Social Media platforms for

ensuring timely and accurate information to the applicants under the 
provisions of the Act, vocalizes effective containment of First and 
Second Appeals in compliance with the letter and spirit of the Right

Annexure- II
Annual Report on CSR Activities for FY25-26
1. Brief outline on CSR Policy of the Company:
 RITES CSR Policy
 Introduction
 i. RITES Ltd., (‘RITES’ or ‘Company’) a Government of India 
Enterprise was established in 1974, under the aegis of 
Indian Railways. RITES is incorporated in India as a Public 
Limited Company under the Companies Act, 2013 and is 
governed by a Board of Directors which includes persons 
of eminence from various sectors of engineering and 
management. RITES provides a comprehensive array of 
services under a single roof. In overseas projects, RITES 
actively pursues and develops cooperative links with 
local consultants/ firms, as means of maximum utilization 
of local resources and as an effective instrument of 
sharing its expertise.
 ii. Over the years, RITES has made significant contributions 
towards society by working in remote areas under 
arduous conditions and at lower fee for the development 
of remote areas, undertaking construction management 
projects, rural road, and rural electrification projects. 
Professional integrity and total transparency are the 
hallmarks of RITES practice of Corporate Governance. 
RITES promotes the cause of Sustainable Development 
and gives due attention to social and environmental 
aspects and their impacts in all its studies, investigations, 
designs & DPRs.
 iii. RITES Corporate Social Responsibility & Sustainability 
Policy (‘Policy’), is based on the CSR policy framework 
laid down in Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 
(‘the Act’) and in accordance with the Companies 
(Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014 as 
amended & (‘the Rules’) notified by Ministry of Corporate 
Affairs, Government of India and the Guidelines on 
Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability for 
Central Public Sector Enterprises, 2014 issued by the 
Department of Public Enterprises, Government of India 
(‘DPE Guidelines'). 
 Definitions
 In this Policy, unless otherwise specified, all capitalized words 
shall have the meaning as provided in the Companies Act, 2013 
and the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility) Policy 
Rules, 2014, as amended.
 Scope
 i. This Policy applies to selection, implementation, 
monitoring, documentation and reporting of CSR and 
sustainability activities undertaken by the Company.
 ii. This Policy does not cover activities undertaken by 
the Company in its normal course of business as well 
as activities exclusively for benefit of employees and/
or their family. iii. This Policy shall apply evenly to all CSR projects or 
programmes undertaken by the Company.
 iv. Any point not covered by this Policy would be interpreted 
in accordance with the existing provisions of Section 135 
of the Act, the Rules and the DPE Guidelines, with the 
former two taking precedence over the latter in cases 
of any conflict.
 v. Any new provision arising out of amendments to 
Companies Act, 2013, the Rules or the DPE Guidelines 
shall apply to this Policy, as if it is specifically 
incorporated in the Policy.
 Vision
 Corporate Social Responsibility Policy is our commitment 
to support initiatives in creating a socially, economically, 
and environmentally sustainable society in a manner that is 
responsible, transparent, and ethical.
 Mission
 To promote and enhance the social, economic, and environmental 
welfare of the society, by working towards providing the 
best possible solutions for sustainable developmental needs, 
by efficient use of resources, green energy initiatives and 
minimising cost and to encourage engagement with the 
stake holders including employees, shareholders, investors, 
customers, clients, business associates, civil society groups, 
Central/State/ local government, communities, environment 
and society at large in determining their needs and expectations.
 Objectives
 i. To support activities/projects listed in Schedule VII of the 
Act by giving priority to issue which are foremost concern 
in the national development agenda, like safe drinking 
water for all, provision of toilets especially for girls, health 
and sanitation, education, etc.
 ii. To promote sustainable development and inclusive 
growth, and to address the basic needs of the deprived, 
under privileged, neglected, and weaker sections of the 
society which comprise of SC, ST, OBCs, minorities, 
BPL families, old and aged, women/girl child, physically 
challenged, etc.
 iii. Promoting the cause of Sustainable Development 
and giving due attention to social and environmental 
aspects and their impacts in all its activities including the 
feasibility studies, investigations, detailed designs & DPRs 
for various developmental projects in transportation & 
infrastructure sector.
 iv. Encouraging use of renewable energy resources such 
as solar, wind, biomass & others and reduce its carbon, 
water, and waste footprints.
=== page 93 ===
Corporate Overview Financial Statements Statutory Reports
Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 73
 v. Engaging stakeholders in undertaking CSR projects in 
and around the areas of Company’s offices/projects and 
other backward regions/areas with focus on creating the 
necessary infrastructure which will promote education, 
health, sanitation and provide connectivity/mobility, skills.
 vi. Spreading awareness amongst employees about the 
Company’s CSR Policy, various programs & initiatives, and 
the need for and importance of adopting ethical business 
practices and implementation of CSR of the Company.
 vii. To adhere to the global standards in CSR practices and 
keep in mind the UN Global Compact and the UN SDGs.
 viii. To promote responsible behaviour by encouraging 
production of goods and services which are safe and 
healthy for the consumers and the environment, resource 
efficient, consumer friendly. ix. To ensure that employees at all levels understand and 
imbibe the philosophy and spirit of CSR and get embedded 
in the core values of the Company.
 x. To devise a communication strategy for regular dialogue 
and consultation with key stakeholders to ascertain 
their views and suggestions regarding the CSR activities 
initiatives undertaken by the Company and making regular 
reports of CSR performance of the Company.
 xi. To implement the Policy by ensuring compliance to legal & 
regulatory requirements and the Act, the Rules, the DPE 
Guidelines, Government guidelines or circulars issued 
from time to time.

 Impact Assessment & Feedback from Beneficiaries
 i. To determine the degree of success and effectiveness 
of the Company’s CSR initiatives, an impact assessment 
shall be carried out by the Company having average 
CSR obligation of 10 crore or more in pursuance of 
sub-section (5) of section 135 of the Act, in the three 
immediately preceding financial years. The impact 
assessment shall be undertaken through an independent 
agency, of CSR projects having outlays of 1 Crore or more, 
and which have been completed not less than one year 
before undertaking the impact study. A survey shall be 
=== page 94 ===
RITES Limited 74
conducted to assess the impact of CSR project in terms of 
social, economic, and environmental benefits accrued to 
the intended beneficiaries. The impact assessment report 
shall be placed before the Board of the Company and shall 
be annexed to the Annual Report on CSR.
 ii. All the CSR projects/activities are undertaken with 
anticipated impact on society and environment. Against 
these perceptions and expectations of impact that 
the completed activity/project should be measured to 
ascertain the degree of the success, or failure. Impact 
assessment is not only concerned with the mere outputs 
or outcomes involving accomplishment of set targets and 
goals at various stages of progress in implementation 
but the cumulative effect of these outcome(s) on the 
developmental process affecting society, economy 
and environment.
 iii. The survey is conducted through the means of a 
structured questionnaire designed keeping in mind the 
prior data of baseline survey or need assessment study. 
The stakeholders are interviewed during the site visits 
and their responses are recorded to gauge the impact 
of the CSR projects in their social, environment and 
economic well-being.
 iv. The surveys shall be done by the RITES CSR Cell either by 
own staff or through the help of an external agency. The 
requirements highlighted during the need assessment 
study and the proposed benefits and impacts are verified 
against the ground level conditions and the beneficial 
impacts seen/felt by the stakeholders.
 v. The local community, stakeholders are involved in 
feedback via surveys, interactions during site visits 
and their involvement in the day-to-day operations 
and assessment of further developmental needs. It is 
recognized that the impact assessment shall be qualitative 
in nature and exact quantification of the benefits accrued 
may be difficult to be ascertained. The sample size 
selected for impact assessment shall be representative of 
the population and would include the officials of local/
district administration, NGOs, SHGs, gram panchayats, 
gram sabhas, local councilors and other members of local 
community both young and old, gents and ladies, boys 
and girls to the extent possible.
 vi. The report of impact assessment shall include: (i) Name, 
address and contact details of the person/household surveyed; (ii) The parameters on which the impact 
assessment is based; (iii) The status in terms of then and 
now; (iv) Photographs of the group meeting/ community 
engagement along with the date and location; (v) 
Photographic or narrative description of improvement; 
(vi) Details of survey team members and their role in 
the survey; (vii) Brief summary about the new initiatives 
which can be taken up further.
 vii. The report shall be scrutinized, analyzed for deficiencies, 
if any, by the CSR Cell and salient features shall be brought 
to the notice of board level committee. The report shall 
form one of the basis for further improvement in the 
Company’s CSR initiative. The impact assessment results 
shall be a part of the annual CSR Report.
 viii. The expenditure incurred by the Company for undertaking 
impact assessment may be booked towards Corporate 
Social Responsibility for that financial year, which shall not 
exceed 2% of the total CSR expenditure for the financial 
year or H50 lakh, whichever is higher.

Government of India. RITES has established a sound framework of Corporate Governance. Its commitment 
to follow good corporate governance practice is based upon transparency, fairness, conscience, teamwork, 
professionalism and accountability, paving the way for following the best standards and building confidence 
among all the stakeholders which is necessary to achieve its overall objectives.
The Company is adhering to the provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations,

1. Company’s Philosophy
 The philosophy of the Company in relation to Corporate Governance is to ensure transparency in 
all its operations, make required disclosures and timely reporting to stock exchanges that conforms 
fully to laws, rules & regulations and guidelines and to promote ethical conduct throughout the 
organization with the primary objective of enhancing the shareholders’ value.
Corporate Governance is critical for enhancing and retaining investors’ trust. Corporate Governance 
facilitates efficient and effective management and is all about maintaining a valuable relationship with 
stakeholders. Corporate Governance is a journey incorporating sustainable value creation and maximizing 
stakeholders value. Corporate Governance also provides competitive edge in the dynamic environment 
and establishes a climate of trust and creativity among its various constituents by making all necessary 
disclosures, complying with all the laws of land and creation of wealth legally and ethically.
RITES believes in promoting the principles of sound Corporate Governance and its essential character 
is shaped by high standard of transparency, trust and integrity, performance orientation, responsibility, 
accountability, professionalism, social responsiveness and ethical business practices. RITES lays special Report on Corporate

like Rail Transport/ Infrastructure will have an added advantage.

projects discipline, he is expected to direct and provide technical guidelines to the various 
consultancy service group.

3. Code of Insider Trading
 Board has laid down “The Code of Internal Procedures and 
Conduct for Prohibition of Insider Trading in Dealing with the 
Securities” in pursuance of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider 
Trading) Regulations, 2015, with an aim that ‘Designated 
Persons’ shall not derive any benefit or assist others to derive 
any benefit from the access to and possession of Unpublished 
Price Sensitive Information about the Company which is not available in the public domain and thus constitutes insider 
information. Company Secretary has been designated as 
Compliance Officer for this Code.
 The Company is adhering to all the requirements as per the 
SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 and the amendments thereto. 
All the reports and disclosures as required under the code, 
have been provided to the Audit Committee from time to 
time. The Company is also monitoring the trades done by the 
Designated Persons and their immediate relatives on a regular 
basis to ensure no deviation from the code is observed. In 
case of default requisite penalties are imposed on designated 
persons as per Insider Trading Code of the Company and the 
amount recovered as penalty is transferred to designated 
SEBI IPEF Account.

4.2. Nomination and Remuneration Committee:
 RITES Limited, being a Government Company, its directors are 
appointed by the Hon’ble President of India through Ministry 
of Railways and they draw remuneration as determined by the 
Government of India and as per the terms and conditions of 
their appointment and as amended from time to time. The Company has constituted Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee in line with the requirements of Section 178 of 
the Companies Act, 2013, the provisions of the SEBI (LODR) 
Regulations, 2015 and the Guidelines on Corporate Governance 
for Central Public Sector Enterprises issued by the Department 
of Public Enterprises (DPE). 
 Performance Evaluation of Directors:
 The requirement of specifying the manner for effective 
evaluation of performance of Board, its Committees and 
individual directors to be carried out either by the Board, by the 
Nomination and Remuneration Committee or by an independent 
external agency under Section 178(2) of the Companies Act, 
2013 has been done away with for Government Companies 
vide Ministry of Corporate Affairs’ (MCA) notification 
dated June 5, 2015.
 Further, MCA vide its notification dated July 5, 2017 has made 
an amendment in the Schedule IV of the Companies Act, 
2013 whereby it has exempted Government Companies from 
complying with the requirement of performance evaluation 
by the Independent Director of Non-Independent Directors 
and Chairman and performance evaluation of the Independent 
Directors by the Board, if the concerned departments or 
ministries have specified these requirements.

 Scope of the Committee:
 The scope and function of the Stakeholders Relationship 
Committee is in line with the provisions of Section 178 (5) of 
the Companies Act, 2013 and Regulation 20 of the SEBI (LODR) 
Regulations, 2015. The scope of the Committee is to specifically 
consider and resolve the grievances of the shareholders 
including the complaints related to transfer of shares, non-
receipt of Annual Reports, dividends etc.
 The role of the Committee inter-alia includes the following:
 1. Resolving the grievances of the security holders 
including complaints related to transfer/transmission 
of shares, non-receipt of annual report, non-receipt of 
declared dividends, issue of new/duplicate certificates, 
general meetings etc.
 2. Review of measures taken for effective exercise of voting 
rights by shareholders.
 3. Review of adherence to the service standards adopted 
by the listed entity in respect of various services being 
rendered by the Registrar & Share Transfer Agent.  4. Review of the various measures and initiatives taken by 
the listed entity for reducing the quantum of unclaimed 
dividends and ensuring timely receipt of dividend 
warrants/annual reports/statutory notices by the 
shareholders of the Company.

 Terms of Reference:
 The terms of reference of the Risk Management Committee 
are as follows:
 1. To formulate a detailed risk management policy 
which shall include:
  a) A Framework for identification of internal and 
external risks specifically faced by the listed 
entity, in particular including financial, operational, 
sectoral, sustainability (particularly ESG related 
risks), information, cyber security risks or any other 
risk as may be determined by the Committee.
  b) Measures for risk mitigation including systems and 
processes for internal control of identified risks.
  c) Business continuity plan.
 2. To ensure that appropriate methodology, processes 
and systems are in place to monitor and evaluate risks 
associated with the business of the Company.
 3. To monitor and oversee implementation of the risk 
management policy, including evaluating the adequacy of 
risk management systems.
 4. To periodically review the risk management policy, 
including by considering the changing industry dynamics 
and evolving complexity. 5. To keep the Board of Directors informed about the nature 
and content of its discussions, recommendations and 
actions to be taken.
 6. The appointment, removal and terms of remuneration of 
the Chief Risk Officer (if any) shall be subject to review by 
the Risk Management Committee.
 7. Evaluating, reviewing, recommending (to Board of 
Directors) and monitoring the Risk Management Plan for 
effective implementation.
 8. Suggest measures for any crisis situation, whether actual 
or anticipated, that may lead to business interruption of 
the company, on immediate and priority basis.
